title: fix: inbox search ignores notification body text
body:
## Problem

The inbox search box only matches the notification title. Any query that appears in the message body returns no results, so users cannot find a notification by what it said.

**Affected area:** notifications / search

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/domain/notification_query.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Launch the app and open the **Inbox** tab.
3. Confirm that the fixture notification titled `Payment received` is visible and that its body reads `Your UPI transaction of INR 2,400 was credited successfully.`
4. Type `UPI` into the search field.

## Expected result

The `Payment received` notification is listed, because `UPI` appears in its body.

## Actual result

No results are shown. The list is blank and the counter reads `0 notifications`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Searching matches text in the notification title **or** the body.
- [ ] Matching stays case insensitive.
- [ ] A query containing a SQL wildcard (`%` or `_`) is treated as literal text, not as a wildcard.
- [ ] An empty or whitespace-only query still returns every notification.

## Testing

- `test/features/notifications/notification_repository_test.dart`: add a case asserting a body-only match is returned.
- Add a case asserting a query matching neither field returns nothing.
- Add a case asserting `%` in a query does not match everything.

## Difficulty

Beginner

## Where to look

`NotificationQuery.where` builds the clause `title LIKE ?`.

---

title: fix: date range filter excludes the final selected day
body:
## Problem

The upper bound of a date range is compared against midnight at the *start* of the chosen end date, so every notification posted on that final day is filtered out. The same builder powers the Statistics screen, so `Last 7 days` silently drops today as well.

**Affected area:** notifications / filtering, statistics

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/domain/notification_query.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Inbox** tab and tap the filter icon.
3. Under **Date range**, select a range that starts yesterday and ends today, then tap **Show results**.
4. Observe which notifications are listed.
5. Open the **Stats** tab with `Last 7 days` selected and look at the `Volume per day` chart.

## Expected result

Notifications posted today are included in the filtered inbox, and today appears as a bar in the statistics chart.

## Actual result

Everything posted today is missing from both screens. Only notifications up to midnight of the end date are counted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A range whose end date is today includes everything posted today.
- [ ] A single-day range (start == end) returns that whole day.
- [ ] The lower bound still includes everything from the start date's 00:00.
- [ ] The Statistics screen counts today when the selected range includes it.

## Testing

- Add a repository test inserting a notification at 23:59 on the end date and assert it is returned.
- Add a test for a same-day range.
- Add a statistics test asserting today's notifications are counted by `Last 7 days`.

## Difficulty

Intermediate

## Where to look

Compare the end bound against `endOfDay`, not `startOfDay`. `DateTimeX` already provides both.

---

title: fix: application totals double when two rules target the same app
body:
## Problem

`ApplicationRepository.summaries()` joins `rules` in order to show how many rules target an app. The join multiplies notification rows, so every notification is counted once per matching rule. An app with two enabled package rules reports twice its real total.

**Affected area:** applications / grouping

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/applications/data/application_repository.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Apps** tab.
3. Note the count shown for **Fixture Chat** (the fixtures ship two enabled rules that both target `com.example.chat`).
4. Tap Fixture Chat to open its detail screen and count the notifications actually listed.

## Expected result

The total on the Applications row equals the number of notifications listed on the app's detail screen.

## Actual result

The Applications row reports double the real total (and double the unread count). Apps with one rule or none are correct, which is why the problem looks intermittent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `total` and `unread` are independent of how many rules match the application.
- [ ] `matchingRules` still reports the number of enabled package rules.
- [ ] `lastPostedAt` stays correct.
- [ ] The query still returns applications that have no notifications at all, with a total of 0.

## Testing

- Extend `test/features/applications/application_repository_test.dart` with a case that inserts two enabled rules for one package and asserts the total is unchanged.
- Assert `matchingRules` equals 2 in that same case.

## Difficulty

Intermediate

## Where to look

Either count distinct notification ids, or compute the rule count in a separate subquery instead of a join.

---

title: fix: unread counter does not refresh after deleting a notification
body:
## Problem

`InboxNotifier.delete` removes the row and updates the list, but never invalidates `unreadCountProvider`. The Dashboard and the inbox app bar keep showing the old unread total until something else happens to refresh it.

**Affected area:** notifications / state management

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Dashboard** tab and note the number on the **Unread** card.
3. Switch to the **Inbox** tab, long-press an unread notification and choose **Delete**.
4. Go back to the **Dashboard** tab without pulling to refresh.

## Expected result

The Unread card drops by one immediately after the deletion.

## Actual result

The Unread card still shows the old value. Pulling to refresh corrects it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deleting an unread notification updates the unread count everywhere it is shown.
- [ ] Deleting a notification that was already read leaves the count unchanged.
- [ ] `deleteMany` behaves the same way as `delete`.
- [ ] No extra database query is issued when nothing was deleted.

## Testing

- Add a provider test that reads `unreadCountProvider`, deletes an unread notification through `inboxProvider`, and asserts the count decreases.
- Add the equivalent test for `deleteMany`.

## Difficulty

Beginner

## Where to look

Compare `delete` with `archive` in the same file; `archive` already does the right thing.

---

title: fix: snoozed notifications reappear before their snooze time
body:
## Problem

The snooze clause compares `snooze_until` against the *end of today* instead of the current time. Any snooze that expires later the same day is treated as already elapsed, so the notification is never actually hidden.

**Affected area:** notifications / snooze

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/domain/notification_query.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Inbox** tab.
3. Long-press any notification, choose **Snooze**, then choose **15 minutes**.
4. The row disappears from the list because the notifier removes it locally.
5. Pull down to refresh the inbox, or switch tabs and come back.

## Expected result

The notification stays out of the inbox for 15 minutes and appears under **Snoozed** (the clock icon in the app bar) in the meantime.

## Actual result

The notification is back in the inbox immediately after the refresh, while the Snoozed screen correctly still lists it as snoozed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A notification snoozed for any duration stays out of the inbox until its snooze time has passed.
- [ ] A notification whose snooze time has passed appears in the inbox again.
- [ ] Notifications that were never snoozed are unaffected.
- [ ] The Snoozed screen and the inbox agree on what is snoozed.

## Testing

- Add a repository test that snoozes a notification by one hour and asserts `page()` does not return it.
- Add a test that snoozes by a negative duration (already expired) and asserts it *is* returned.
- Add a test asserting a snoozed notification appears in `snoozed()` and not in `all()` at the same time.

## Difficulty

Intermediate

## Where to look

The clause is appended at the end of `NotificationQuery.where`. The bound should be `DateTime.now()`.

---

title: fix: no empty state when a search returns no results
body:
## Problem

The inbox only renders its empty state when the search query is empty. A search with no matches therefore shows a blank area with no explanation and no way to recover.

**Affected area:** notifications / UI

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/presentation/inbox_page.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Inbox** tab.
3. Type `zzzzz` into the search field.

## Expected result

A clear empty state explains that no notifications match the search, and offers a way to clear it.

## Actual result

The list area is blank. Only the `0 notifications match your filters` line hints at what happened.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An empty result set always shows an empty state.
- [ ] The wording distinguishes "nothing captured yet" from "nothing matches your search or filters".
- [ ] When filters or a search caused the empty result, the empty state offers an action that clears them.
- [ ] The empty state is reachable by a screen reader.

## Testing

- Extend `test/widgets/inbox_page_test.dart` with a case that types a non-matching query and asserts `EmptyState` is present.
- Add a case asserting the clear action restores the full list.

## Difficulty

See the `items.isEmpty && searchQuery.isEmpty` condition in `_InboxList.build`.

title: fix: inbox pagination skips one notification per page
body:
## Problem

`InboxNotifier.loadMore` passes `current.items.length + 1` as the SQL offset. The `+ 1` skips exactly one notification at every page boundary, so records silently disappear from the inbox as the user scrolls.

**Affected area:** notifications / pagination

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/presentation/providers/notification_providers.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Inbox** tab (the fixtures contain more than 60 notifications, and the page size is 20).
3. Note the 20th and 21st notifications by scrolling slowly.
4. Keep scrolling so the next page loads.
5. Compare the list against `SELECT title, posted_at FROM notification_items ORDER BY posted_at DESC` or against the per-app lists on the Apps tab.

## Expected result

Scrolling through the whole inbox shows every notification exactly once; the number of rows matches the counter above the list.

## Actual result

One notification is skipped at each page boundary, so the inbox shows fewer rows than the counter claims.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Paging through the entire list yields every notification exactly once, in order.
- [ ] No notification is returned twice.
- [ ] `hasMore` becomes false exactly once, after the last page.
- [ ] Paging still works when the total is an exact multiple of the page size.

## Testing

- Add a repository or notifier test that inserts 25 notifications, loads two pages and asserts the collected ids equal the ids from an unpaged query.
- Add a case where the total is exactly 20 and assert `hasMore` ends up false with no duplicate fetch.

## Difficulty

Intermediate

## Where to look

A SQL `OFFSET` is the number of rows to skip, which is exactly the number of rows already loaded.

---

title: fix: statistics total ignores the active filters
body:
## Problem

`StatisticsRepository.load` computes `total` with a query that hard-codes `WHERE is_archived = 0` and drops the filter entirely, while every breakdown below it respects the filter. The headline number therefore contradicts the chart underneath it.

**Affected area:** statistics

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/statistics/data/statistics_repository.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Stats** tab.
3. Select `Last 7 days`, then pick a single application such as **Fixture Team** from the second chip row.
4. Compare the **Total notifications** card with the sum of the bars in **Volume per day** and with the per-application breakdown.

## Expected result

The Total notifications card equals the sum of the filtered breakdowns.

## Actual result

The total stays at the all-time, all-apps count and does not change when the range or the application filter changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `total` respects the range, the application filter and every other field of `NotificationFilter`.
- [ ] `total` equals the sum of `perDay` counts for the same filter.
- [ ] `total` equals the sum of `perPriority` counts for the same filter.
- [ ] An empty result set reports a total of 0 rather than the table size.

## Testing

- Add a statistics test asserting `total` changes when a package filter is applied.
- Add a test asserting `total` equals the summed `perDay` counts.

## Difficulty

Intermediate

## Where to look

The filtered clause is already built in `load()` as `where`/`args`; the total query just does not use it.

title: fix: notifications with identical timestamps sort inconsistently
body:
## Problem

`page()` orders only by `posted_at DESC`, with no tiebreaker, while `all()` and `forPackage()` order by `posted_at DESC, id DESC`. Notifications that share a timestamp therefore appear in a different order in the inbox than in the per-app list, and SQLite is free to return them in a different order between two paged queries, which can also duplicate or drop rows at a page boundary.

**Affected area:** notifications / sorting

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/data/notification_repository.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. The fixtures contain two notifications posted at exactly 14:00 today: `Build passed` (Fixture Team) and `Weekly report is ready` (Fixture Mail).
3. Open the **Inbox** tab and note which of the two is listed first.
4. Open the **Apps** tab, open **Fixture Team**, then open **Fixture Mail**, and compare their relative order against the inbox.
5. Pull to refresh the inbox a few times and watch the two rows.

## Expected result

Two notifications with the same timestamp keep one stable, documented order in every list and across refreshes.

## Actual result

The inbox order of the tied pair is not guaranteed and can differ from the per-app lists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every notification query uses the same deterministic sort, including a tiebreaker.
- [ ] Repeating the same query returns the same order.
- [ ] The inbox and the per-app list agree on the order of tied notifications.
- [ ] The sort order is stated in a doc comment on the repository.

## Testing

- Add a repository test that inserts two notifications with identical `postedAt` and asserts `page()` returns them in the same order as `all()`.
- Add a test that runs the same paged query twice and asserts identical id order.

## Difficulty

Intermediate

## Where to look

Put the ordering in one constant used by every query in the repository.

---

title: fix: retention setting is not restored after restart
body:
## Problem

`SettingsRepository.saveRetentionDays` writes to `PrefKeys.retentionDays` (`settings.retention_days`), but `load()` reads a hard-coded `'settings.retentionDays'`. The two keys never match, so the stored value is unreachable and the setting falls back to its default on every launch.

**Affected area:** settings / persistence

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/settings/data/settings_repository.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Settings** tab.
3. Under **Data**, tap **Keep history for** and choose `90 days`. The subtitle updates to `90 days`.
4. Fully restart the app (stop and relaunch, not hot reload).
5. Open **Settings** again.

## Expected result

`Keep history for` still reads `90 days`.

## Actual result

It has reverted to `30 days`. Every other setting on the screen is restored correctly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A saved retention value is read back after a restart.
- [ ] Every preference is read and written through a key defined in `PrefKeys`, with no string literals.
- [ ] An absent value still falls back to `AppConstants.defaultRetentionDays`.
- [ ] `Forever` (0) round-trips and is not confused with "not set".

## Testing

- Extend `test/features/settings/settings_repository_test.dart` with a save-then-load round trip for retention.
- Add a case asserting `0` round-trips as `Forever`.

## Difficulty

Beginner

## Where to look

`PrefKeys` carries a comment saying every key must go through it. One call site does not.

---

title: fix: muting an application does not remove it from the inbox
body:
## Problem

`app_sources.is_muted` is persisted and shown in the UI, but no notification query consults it. Muting an app changes the switch and nothing else, even though the documented behaviour is that a muted app keeps collecting history while staying out of the inbox.

**Affected area:** applications / notifications

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/domain/notification_query.dart`
- `lib/features/applications/data/application_repository.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Apps** tab and turn the switch **off** for **Fixture Chat** (off means muted).
3. Go to the **Inbox** tab and pull to refresh.

## Expected result

Fixture Chat notifications are no longer listed in the inbox, while remaining visible on the Fixture Chat detail screen and counted in Statistics.

## Actual result

Fixture Chat notifications are still in the inbox. Only the mute icon on the Apps row changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The inbox excludes notifications from muted applications.
- [ ] The per-application detail screen still shows them.
- [ ] Unmuting restores them in the inbox without data loss.
- [ ] The behaviour is documented on the mute switch (a subtitle or tooltip).
- [ ] Decide and document whether the unread badge counts muted apps.

## Testing

- Add a repository test that mutes an app and asserts `page()` excludes its notifications while `forPackage()` includes them.
- Add a test that unmutes and asserts they return.

## Difficulty

The inbox query will need to consider `app_sources`. Keep one source of truth for the clause so the inbox and the counter cannot disagree.

title: fix: "mark all as read" ignores the active filter
body:
## Problem

`markAllAsRead` accepts a `NotificationFilter` and then ignores it, running `UPDATE notification_items SET is_read = 1 WHERE is_read = 0` across the whole table. A user who filters to one app and taps the button marks their entire history as read, with no undo.

**Affected area:** notifications

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/data/notification_repository.dart`

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a **debug build**, open **Settings > Developer > Load issue fixtures**. SignalBox ships no sample data - it shows your own captured notifications - so the fixtures give every contributor the same starting point.
2. Open the **Inbox** tab and confirm several apps have unread notifications.
3. Tap the filter icon, select only **Fixture Team** under **Application**, and tap **Show results**.
4. Tap the double-tick **Mark all as read** button in the app bar.
5. Clear the filter.

## Expected result

Only the Fixture Team notifications that matched the filter are marked read; everything else stays unread.

## Actual result

Every notification in the database is marked read, including archived ones and ones from other apps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only notifications matching the active filter are marked as read.
- [ ] With no filter active, the behaviour is unchanged (everything unread becomes read).
- [ ] Archived notifications are only affected when `includeArchived` is set.
- [ ] The unread counter and the list both refresh afterwards.

## Testing

- Add a repository test that marks all read under a package filter and asserts other packages stay unread.
- Add a test asserting archived rows are untouched by default.

## Difficulty

Intermediate

## Where to look

`NotificationQuery.where` already produces the clause; `markAllAsRead` just needs to use it.

title: feat: export notification history to CSV
body:
## Problem

SignalBox is local-first and deliberately has no backend, which means users currently have no way to get their own data out of the app. There is no export, so the history cannot be analysed elsewhere or kept after an uninstall.

**Affected area:** settings / data

## Current state

Settings > Data > **Export history to CSV** exists and shows a "not implemented yet" snackbar.

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/settings/presentation/settings_page.dart`
- `lib/features/notifications/data/notification_repository.dart`

## User story

> As a SignalBox user I want to export my notification history as a CSV file so that I can analyse it in a spreadsheet and keep a copy outside the app.

## Functional requirements

- Export every notification matching the filter the user chooses: all history, or the currently active inbox filter.
- Columns: `posted_at` (ISO 8601 local time), `package_name`, `app_label`, `title`, `body`, `priority`, `category`, `is_read`, `is_archived`.
- Escape the CSV correctly: quote fields containing commas, quotes or newlines, and double embedded quotes.
- Write the file to a user-visible location and offer the system share sheet.
- Show progress for large exports and keep the UI responsive.
- Report the row count and the file path on success; show a recoverable error on failure.

## Expected UI behaviour

A bottom sheet offering **All notifications** or **Current filter**, then a progress indicator, then a snackbar with the result and a **Share** action.

## Technical considerations

- Stream rows from SQLite instead of loading everything into memory; add a repository method that returns an iterable/stream.
- Use `path_provider` for the target directory; no new dependency is required for CSV writing.
- Do the string building in an isolate (`compute`) if a benchmark shows it blocking the frame budget.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exporting produces a file that opens in a spreadsheet with one header row and one row per notification.
- [ ] A notification whose body contains a comma, a double quote and a newline survives a round trip through the CSV.
- [ ] Exporting an empty history produces a file with only the header row and says so, rather than failing.
- [ ] The export runs off the UI thread; the screen does not freeze for a 10,000-row export.
- [ ] The success message names the file location.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the CSV encoder: commas, quotes, newlines, empty fields, unicode.
- A repository test for the streaming query.
- A widget test asserting the export sheet appears and the success message is shown.

## Difficulty

Intermediate

title: feat: apply notification rules to incoming notifications
body:
## Problem

The whole point of the Rules screen is to automate priority and categorisation, but no evaluation engine exists. Rules are inert data, so users have to triage every notification by hand.

**Affected area:** rules / core

## Current state

Rules can be created, edited, enabled and deleted, and are persisted. A banner on the Rules screen states they are not applied. `RuleAction` and `RuleMatchField` are defined but nothing evaluates them.

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/rules/data/rule_repository.dart`
- `lib/core/services/notification_access_service.dart`

## User story

> As a SignalBox user I want my rules applied to notifications as they arrive so that important notifications are prioritised and categorised without me touching them.

## Functional requirements

- Evaluate enabled rules in `sortOrder` order against every incoming notification.
- Support all four actions: set priority, assign category, mute the application, auto-snooze for N minutes.
- Support all three match fields: package name, title, body.
- Define and document the semantics of multiple matches (first match wins, or last writer wins per action).
- Matching must be case insensitive and must treat the stored value as literal text, not a pattern.
- A rule referring to a deleted category must not break ingestion.
- Offer a **Test rule** affordance that reports how many stored notifications a rule would match.
- Remove the "not applied" banner once the engine is live.

## Expected UI behaviour

No new screen. The Rules screen loses its warning banner and gains a **Test rule** button showing the match count.

## Technical considerations

- Put the evaluation in a pure `RuleEngine` class in `lib/features/rules/domain/` that takes a notification plus a rule list and returns the resulting values. Keep the database out of it so it can be unit-tested.
- Call the engine from the ingestion path that consumes `NotificationAccessService.stream()`.
- Think about ordering: rules are evaluated once at ingestion. Decide and document whether editing a rule re-applies it to existing history (a separate follow-up is fine).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new notification matching an enabled `setPriority` rule is stored with that priority.
- [ ] A notification matching an `assignCategory` rule is stored with that category id.
- [ ] A notification from an app muted by a rule is stored in history but kept out of the inbox.
- [ ] An `autoSnooze` rule stores a `snooze_until` N minutes in the future.
- [ ] Disabled rules never apply.
- [ ] Rule evaluation is pure and unit-tested without a database.
- [ ] Ingestion still succeeds when a rule's target category no longer exists.

## Testing

- Unit tests for `RuleEngine` covering every action and match field, plus no-match and multi-match cases.
- A test asserting disabled rules are skipped.
- An integration test through the repository asserting a stored notification carries the rule's effects.

title: feat: bulk notification management with multi-select
body:
## Problem

Clearing out a backlog means repeating a long-press and a menu tap for every notification. There is no way to act on many at once, which makes the app impractical after a few days of capture.

**Affected area:** notifications

## Current state

`NotificationRepository.deleteMany` and `InboxNotifier.deleteMany` exist and are tested. Nothing in the UI can select more than one notification.

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/presentation/inbox_page.dart`

## User story

> As a SignalBox user I want to select several notifications and act on them in one go so that I can clear a backlog quickly.

## Functional requirements

- Enter selection mode from a long-press or an explicit **Select** action.
- Select and deselect individual rows, plus **Select all** for the current filtered view.
- Bulk actions: mark read, mark unread, archive, snooze, delete.

- Hold the selected ids in a `Notifier<Set<int>>` so the list rows can watch only what they need.

- [ ] Selecting three notifications and choosing **Archive** archives exactly those three.
- [ ] **Select all** selects every notification matching the active filter, not just the loaded page.

- [ ] A bulk delete can be undone from the snackbar and fully restores the rows.

title: feat: scheduled daily notification summary
body:
## Problem

SignalBox can tell a user how noisy their day was, but only if they open the app. There is no scheduled digest, so the insight never reaches them.

**Affected area:** settings / background work

## Current state

Settings > Privacy > **Daily summary notification** persists a boolean and says scheduling is not wired up. Nothing is scheduled and no summary notification is ever posted.

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/settings/presentation/settings_page.dart`
- `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/signalbox/signalbox/`

## User story

> As a SignalBox user I want a daily summary at a time I choose so that I learn what I missed without opening the app.

## Functional requirements

- Let the user pick the delivery time; default to 21:00 local time.
- Post a local notification summarising the day: total captured, the three busiest apps, and the number of unread high-priority notifications.
- Tapping the summary opens the Statistics screen for today.
- Survive a device reboot (the manifest already declares `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`).
- Respect Android 13+ `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` runtime permission, and request it only when the user enables the feature.
- Turning the setting off cancels any pending work.
- Never include notification body text in the summary, so the digest cannot leak content on a lock screen.

## Expected UI behaviour

A time picker under the toggle, and a subtitle showing the next scheduled delivery.

## Technical considerations

- Use `WorkManager` with a periodic request, or `AlarmManager` with an exact-ish alarm, on the Kotlin side. Discuss the trade-off in the PR: WorkManager is battery friendly but not minute-precise.
- Build the summary text in Dart from the existing `StatisticsRepository` and hand it to the platform side, or query SQLite from Kotlin. Prefer the former to keep one source of truth.
- Add a debug-only **Send summary now** action so the behaviour can be reviewed without waiting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enabling the setting and picking a time schedules exactly one recurring job.
- [ ] The summary arrives at the chosen local time, including after a reboot.
- [ ] The counts in the summary match the Statistics screen for the same day.
- [ ] Disabling the setting cancels the job and no further summaries arrive.
- [ ] Denying the notification permission turns the setting back off and explains why.
- [ ] Daylight-saving and timezone changes do not double-post or skip a day.

## Testing

- Unit test the summary text builder against a fixed statistics payload, including the empty-day case.
- Unit test the scheduling controller with a fake platform channel: enable schedules, disable cancels.
- Document the manual verification steps for reboot and timezone change in the PR.

title: feat: backup and restore the local database
body:
## Problem

Everything SignalBox knows lives in one SQLite file on one device. Changing phones or clearing app data loses the entire history, and there is no supported way to move it.

**Affected area:** settings / data

## Current state

Settings > Data > **Backup and restore** exists and shows a "not implemented yet" snackbar.

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/settings/presentation/settings_page.dart`
- `lib/core/database/app_database.dart`

## User story

> As a SignalBox user I want to back my data up to a file and restore it on another device so that my history survives a phone change.

## Functional requirements

- Export notifications, applications, categories, rules and preferences into a single versioned archive.
- Include a schema version and an app version in the archive, and refuse to restore an archive from a newer schema.
- Restore must either replace the current data or merge it; the choice must be explicit and explained.
- Validate the archive before writing anything, and leave the database untouched if validation fails.
- Restore inside a transaction so a failure cannot leave a half-restored database.
- Warn clearly before a destructive restore.

## Expected UI behaviour

Two entries, **Back up now** and **Restore from file**, a confirmation dialog naming what will be overwritten, and a progress indicator.

## Technical considerations

- Prefer a JSON archive over copying the raw `.sqlite` file: it is inspectable, diffable in review, and portable across schema versions.
- Reuse the migration machinery in `AppDatabase` for older archives.
- Keep ids out of the archive, or remap them on restore, so merge mode cannot collide.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A backup taken on one device restores on another with identical counts in every table.
- [ ] Restoring a truncated or malformed file fails with a clear message and changes nothing.
- [ ] Restoring an archive whose schema version is newer is refused with an explanation.
- [ ] A replace-restore leaves no rows from before the restore.
- [ ] Preferences (theme, retention, privacy) are restored too.

## Testing

- Round-trip test: seed, back up, wipe, restore, assert table contents match.
- Tests for malformed input, a newer schema version and an empty database.
- A test asserting a failed restore rolls back.

## Difficulty

Advanced

title: feat: enforce the configurable data retention window
body:
## Problem

The app promises to keep history for a chosen window, but never deletes anything. The database grows without bound and the setting is decorative. Note this feature is blocked by the retention persistence bug.

**Affected area:** settings / data

## Current state

`NotificationRepository.deleteOlderThan` is implemented and tested. The retention setting is stored and shown in Settings. Nothing ever calls the cleanup.

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/settings/presentation/settings_page.dart`
- `lib/features/notifications/data/notification_repository.dart`

## User story

> As a SignalBox user I want notifications older than my retention window deleted automatically so that the app does not grow forever and old content does not linger on my device.

## Functional requirements

- Run the cleanup on app start and then at most once a day.
- Never delete anything when the setting is `Forever` (0).
- Report what was removed: show the number of deleted notifications in Settings as a last-run summary.
- Lowering the retention window takes effect on the next cleanup, and the destructive consequence is explained before the value is saved.
- Do not block the first frame on cleanup.

## Expected UI behaviour

A subtitle under **Keep history for** reading e.g. `Last cleanup removed 42 notifications`, plus a confirmation dialog when shortening the window.

## Technical considerations

- Store the last-run timestamp in `SharedPreferences` with a key added to `PrefKeys`.
- Depends on the retention persistence bug being fixed first; otherwise the window always reads as the default.
- Invalidate the inbox, counters and statistics providers after a cleanup that deleted rows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With retention set to 7 days, notifications older than 7 days are gone after a restart and newer ones remain.
- [ ] With `Forever` selected, nothing is deleted.
- [ ] The cleanup runs at most once per calendar day even across several app starts.
- [ ] Choosing a shorter window shows a confirmation that states roughly how many notifications it will remove.
- [ ] Start-up time is not measurably affected.

## Testing

- A test asserting rows past the cutoff are deleted and others are kept.
- A test asserting `Forever` deletes nothing.
- A test asserting the once-a-day guard prevents a second run.

Intermediate

title: feat: per-application analytics screen
body:
## Problem

A user can see that an app is noisy overall but not when it is noisy, or whether it got worse. There is no per-app trend, busiest hour or week-on-week comparison.

**Affected area:** statistics / applications

## Current state

- Show notifications per day for the last 30 days, the busiest hour of the day, the split by priority and category, and the change against the previous period.
- Show the quiet hours during which this app never notifies.
- Offer a **Mute this app** action from the insights view.

title: feat: search improvements - recent searches and match highlighting
body:
## Problem

Every keystroke runs a new query, nothing shows the user why a row matched, and a search has to be retyped from scratch every time.

**Affected area:** notifications / search

## Current state

Search is a plain text field that filters as you type. There is no history, no highlighting and no debounce.

**Likely files**

- `lib/features/notifications/presentation/inbox_page.dart`

## User story

> As a SignalBox user I want my recent searches and highlighted matches so that searching is faster and I can see what matched.

## Functional requirements

- Debounce the query so typing does not issue a query per keystroke.
- Highlight the matched substring in the title and body of each result.
- Keep the last five searches and offer them when the field is focused and empty.
- Let a recent search be removed, and offer **Clear history**.
- Recent searches persist across restarts.

## Expected UI behaviour

A dropdown of recent searches below the field; matched text in a tinted span.

## Technical considerations

- Debounce with a `Timer` in the notifier, not in the widget, so the behaviour is testable.
- Build highlighting with `Text.rich` and `TextSpan` ranges; take care with overlapping or repeated matches.
- Store recent searches as a string list in `SharedPreferences` through a new `PrefKeys` entry.
- Depends on the body-search fix, otherwise highlighting in the body will never have anything to highlight.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Typing `invoice` quickly issues one query rather than seven.
- [ ] The matched substring is visually distinct in the result rows, in both light and dark themes.
- [ ] Highlighting is case insensitive and highlights every occurrence.
- [ ] Recent searches appear when the empty field is focused, and selecting one runs it.
- [ ] Nothing is highlighted when the query is empty.

## Testing

- A unit test for the span builder: no match, one match, several matches, different case, empty query.
- A test asserting the debounce collapses rapid input into one query.
- A test asserting recent searches round-trip through preferences and cap at five.

title: perf: add database indexes for the inbox and statistics queries
body:
## Problem

`notification_items` has no secondary index. Every inbox page sorts the whole table on `posted_at`, every per-app view scans it on `package_name`, and the statistics aggregates scan it repeatedly. This is fine with the 60 fixture rows and poor with months of real capture.

**Affected area:** database

## Requirements

- Measure before changing anything: insert a realistic volume (50,000+ rows) and record the timings of the inbox page query, the per-app query and the statistics aggregates.
- Add the indexes those measurements justify, with a schema migration rather than an edit to the `onCreate` SQL.
- Bump `AppDatabase.schemaVersion` and implement the upgrade branch so existing installs are migrated.
- Re-measure and report the before/after numbers in the pull request.
- Document why each index exists, since every index costs write throughput and disk.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The pull request contains before/after timings from the same machine and dataset.
- [ ] A migration exists and is tested from the current schema version to the new one.
- [ ] A fresh install and an upgraded install end up with identical schemas.
- [ ] `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for the inbox query shows the index being used, and that output is in the PR.
- [ ] No regression in the existing test suite.

## Testing

- A migration test opening a v1 database, upgrading it and asserting the indexes exist.
- A test asserting a fresh install and a migrated install agree on schema.
- A benchmark script or test, excluded from CI, that reproduces the measurement.

title: perf: stop rebuilding the whole inbox list on every state change
body:
## Problem

`_InboxList` watches `appLabelsProvider`, `categoriesByIdProvider` and `settingsProvider` at the top of its build method, so marking one notification read rebuilds every row. Rows are rebuilt whole rather than rebuilding only what changed, and the date headers are recomputed on each build.

**Affected area:** notifications / performance

## Requirements

- Profile first: capture the rebuild counts or a DevTools timeline for marking one notification read in a list of 60.
- Narrow the watches so a row depends only on the data it renders, for example with `select` or a per-row provider.
- Avoid recomputing the grouped row list on every build when the inputs have not changed.
- Keep the widget tree readable: do not trade all clarity for a marginal gain, and say in the PR what the measurement showed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Marking one notification read rebuilds that row and not the rest of the list, demonstrated by a rebuild count or timeline in the PR.
- [ ] Scrolling the fixture inbox holds a steady frame rate in profile mode, with before/after numbers.
- [ ] No behaviour changes: every existing inbox test still passes unmodified.
- [ ] The row widget stays `const`-constructible where its inputs allow it.

## Testing

- A widget test asserting a row is not rebuilt when an unrelated row changes, for instance with a rebuild counter.
- Existing inbox tests must pass without modification.

Intermediate

title: a11y: accessibility pass over the inbox, dashboard and settings
body:
## Problem

Accessibility is partial. `NotificationTile`, `AppAvatar`, `SimpleBarChart` and `BreakdownBar` carry semantics, but icon-only buttons, chips and switches elsewhere do not, several tap targets are below 48dp, and the charts convey information by colour alone.

**Affected area:** accessibility

## Requirements

- Audit the Dashboard, Inbox, Apps, Stats and Settings screens with TalkBack and with the Flutter semantics debugger.
- Give every interactive element an accessible label, and every icon-only button a tooltip.
- Ensure a minimum 48x48dp tap target for every control.
- Check text contrast against WCAG AA in both light and dark themes, especially the muted `onSurfaceVariant` text.
- Make sure nothing relies on colour alone: priority and category must be readable without seeing the colour.
- Verify the layout at 200% font scale without clipping or overflow.
- Write down the findings and the remaining gaps in `docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every interactive element on the audited screens has a meaningful accessible label.
- [ ] No tap target is smaller than 48x48dp.
- [ ] Body and label text meets WCAG AA contrast in both themes, with the measured ratios recorded.
- [ ] At 200% font scale no screen clips or overflows.
- [ ] Priority and category are distinguishable without colour.
- [ ] `docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md` records what was checked, what was fixed and what is still open.

## Testing

- Widget tests using `meetsGuideline(textContrastGuideline)` and `meetsGuideline(androidTapTargetGuideline)` for the audited screens.
- A test pumping a screen at a 2.0 text scale factor and asserting no overflow exception.

title: docs: document the architecture and the data layer contracts
body:
## Problem

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` describes the layout at a high level, but a new contributor still has to read the source to learn how a notification travels from Android to the screen, what each provider is for, or which invariants the repositories guarantee.

**Affected area:** documentation

## Requirements

- Document the full ingestion path: `NotificationListenerService` to `NotificationStreamHandler` to the event channel to the repository to SQLite.
- Document every table and column, including the units of each timestamp and the meaning of each enum index.
- List the providers, what each one owns and which ones must be invalidated after which writes.
- Add dartdoc to every public class and method in `features/*/data` that lacks it, stating the ordering and filtering guarantees.
- Include one diagram of the data flow.
- Explain the testing seams: the `databaseProvider` and `sharedPreferencesProvider` overrides.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A contributor can follow a notification from Android to the inbox using only the docs.
- [ ] Every table and column is documented, with units and enum meanings.
- [ ] `dart doc` produces no warnings for the data layer.
- [ ] The provider invalidation rules are written down in one place.
- [ ] The docs match the code at the time of the pull request, with no references to removed APIs.

## Testing
